newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart plans up to 185 new stores in fiscal 1997.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart plans up to 185 new stores in fiscal 1997.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc., the nation's largest retailer, Tuesday reported sharply higher five-week sales and said it will open up to 185 new stores worldwide in the year beginning Feb. 1, 1997.
The plans include 50 new discount stores in the United States and 30 to 35 in Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China, Indonesia, Mexico and Puerto Rico.

Wal-Mart will also open 100 new U.S. Supercenters, of which about 70 will be relocations or expansions of existing discount stores, the company said. It also plans to open five to 10 new Sam's Clubs member warehouse stores.
The expansion will add about 20 million square feet of retail space to Wal-Mart's U.S. operations, the company said.

Wal-Mart said its net sales for the five weeks ended Oct. 4 jumped 13.2 percent to $9.6 billion from $8.5 billion in the year-ago period. For the 35 weeks ended Oct. 4, sales climbed 11.8 percent to $66.0 billion.
Sam's Clubs sales for the five-week period grew 4.9 percent to $1.8 billion from $1.7 billion. Club sales for the 35 weeks edged up 1.8 percent to $12.7 billion over the year.
Five-week comparable sales rose 6 percent for Wal-Mart, 4.3 percent for Sam's Club and 5.6 percent for the entire Bentonville, Ark.-based retailer, it said.

As of Sept. 30, Wal-Mart had 1,946 Wal-Mart stores, 324 Supercenters, 436 Sam's Clubs, four Argentina units, five Brazilian outlets, 135 Canadian Wal-Mart stores, two China stores, one Indonesian Supercenter, 138 Mexican units and 11 Puerto Rico units.
Wal-Mart's stock rose 50 cents to $27.25 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
